documents.abstract: Résumé La logistique hospitalière (approvisionnement, gestion des stocks, circuit du médicament, distribution interne, transport et déchets) reste souvent traitée comme une simple fonction de soutien, alors qu’elle conditionne la disponibilité des ressources au point de soins. Cet article vise à repositionner cette fonction comme un levier stratégique de transformation des hôpitaux publics. Il s’appuie sur une revue intégrative de la littérature publiée entre 2004 et 2025 (PubMed et moteur de recherche académique Consensus, complétés par une recherche sur le web), centrée sur les établissements publics et sur les contextes africains et marocain, et mobilise trois cadres théoriques : l’approche sociotechnique, le New Public Management et le Balanced Scorecard. L’analyse d’un corpus de 21 publications fait ressortir trois constats. La performance logistique s’organise autour de trois dimensions rarement traitées ensemble : l’efficience économique, l’efficacité opérationnelle et la qualité perçue. Les indicateurs utilisés sont nombreux mais peu harmonisés ; les revues récentes en recensent des dizaines, à dominante financière. Enfin, le Balanced Scorecard reste peu mobilisé dans les hôpitaux publics des pays à revenu faible et intermédiaire, et le vécu des patients et des personnels y est peu pris en compte. L’article propose un modèle intégrateur et un tableau de bord logistique à quatre perspectives, adapté à la réforme du système de santé marocain engagée par la loi-cadre n° 06-22. Mots clés : Logistique hospitalière, Performance, Chaîne d’approvisionnement, Hôpital public, Balanced Scorecard, New Public Management, Maroc. Abstract Hospital logistics (procurement, inventory management, medication circuit, internal distribution, transport and waste) is still often treated as a mere support function, although it determines the availability of resources at the point of care. This article aims to reposition this function as a strategic lever for transforming public hospitals. It draws on an integrative review of literature published between 2004 and 2025 (PubMed and the Consensus academic search engine, supplemented by a web search), focusing on public facilities and on African and Moroccan contexts, and mobilises three theoretical frameworks: the sociotechnical approach, New Public Management and the Balanced Scorecard. The analysis of a corpus of 21 publications yields three findings. Logistics performance is structured around three dimensions that are rarely addressed together: economic efficiency, operational effectiveness and perceived quality. The indicators in use are numerous but poorly harmonised; recent reviews list dozens of them, mostly financial. Finally, the Balanced Scorecard remains little used in public hospitals in low- and middle-income countries, where the experience of patients and staff is seldom considered. The article proposes an integrative model and a four-perspective logistics scorecard adapted to the reform of the Moroccan health system initiated by framework law No. 06-22. Keywords: Hospital logistics, Performance, Supply chain, Public hospital, Balanced Scorecard, New Public Management, Morocco.

At the Seventy-ninth World Health Assembly this year, more than 150 official statements on data, digital health, and artificial intelligence (AI) were delivered by 74 countries and 10 regional blocs, alongside 42 side events, and over 30 Ministers of Health affirming digital transformation as a core feature of resilient health systems. The through line was consistent across every region: countries are calling for concerted global leadership towards shared standards and clear governance to validate, benchmark, and regulate AI in health.Sustainable, effective AI requires an ecosystem to function, and often carries real risks to data sovereignty, privacy, and equity. AI trained on incomplete data, tested in narrow settings, or deployed without attention to bias and local context can reproduce, and even amplify, the very inequities it aims to close. It is against this backdrop that we read the lead article by Guni et al. on "large language medicine (1)." We share the authors' optimism but sharpen their central question: not whether generative and multimodal AI will reshape medicine, but how we build the scaffolding that ensures the reshaping happens safely, equitably, and sustainably.Deep learning, generative AI, large language models (LLMs), and connected agentic systems promise both incremental and transformative change across diagnostics, disease management, surveillance, prevention, and drug discovery. Yet, as Guni et al. candidly note, today's clinically mature, regulator-approved tools remain predominantly diagnostic and built on older machine learning architectures. LLMs have not yet crossed into routine practice; interconnected agentic systems are being introduced only in a fraction of cutting-edge facilities. Health systems and clinical medicine, although a rich proving ground for technical experimentation and innovation, are also understandably cautious and risk averse. The principles of evidence-based medicine further solidify the need for requisite, repeated, and rigorous demonstration of efficacy before well-established practices are altered. Some Author 1 et al. Short title/running header 4 critique this caution as innovation recalcitrance; given the duty of care in health, it is better understood as the scientific scrutiny that any clinical tool, however heavily promoted, should be expected to survive.An AI solution does not scale on its own; it scales when an ecosystem for scale exists or is built around it. This includes clear regulatory capacity and governance, strong health information systems, and trained health personnel. We posit that a key element of that enabling foundation is digital public infrastructure for health. Some of the most durable gains come not from what makes headlines but from the unglamorous parts of the system no one photographs: the unique identifiers and information exchanges, the semantic standards which allow systems to interoperate, powering supply chains that keep essential medicines on the shelf, and persistent records that follow a patient across facilities within a health system to maintain continuity of care. Countries that adopted monolithic, donor-funded digital health tools have already seen those systems collapse when funding shifted; language models deployed as parallel silos, disconnected from a shared reference architecture, risk repeating that failure at greater speed and scale. Technology-neutral reference architectures, developed collaboratively across health and telecommunications agencies and built on open standards, offer a map for where these foundations should sit (2). AI cannot pervade "every aspect of medicine," as Guni et al. envision, without an underlying layer of high-quality data structured for interoperability, disciplined evaluation protocols, and the systems analysis required to introduce AI into existing clinical workflows. Experimental systems may be introduced into clinical practice, but without clear proof points and performance benchmarks, their transition from pilot to clinical standard will likely be slow and inequitable. Ministries and hospital systems are already experiencing a glut of vendors promising impressive solutions to long-standing challenges, often without the accompanying (3,4), or countries with the least regulatory capacity will simply import externally reviewed systems without local ownership. Regulatory sandboxes, such as the United Kingdom's AI Airlock, which allows supervised testing of AI tools that fit no existing device category (5), remain an underused bridge between principle and practice. Harmonization does not mean uniformity; it means enough common evidentiary ground that a safety finding in one country still holds in another, since the models themselves will cross borders faster than any single regulator's jurisdiction can follow. Language, disease burden, health system maturity, and data availability vary enormously; a model validated in one setting cannot be assumed safe in another. Multi-institutional, privacy-preserving evaluation designed into deployment from the start, not bolted on afterward, should be the norm, particularly for populations already under-represented in training data. This brings us to what authentic inclusion in AI design actually looks like. It is not access to a shared global model. It is each country's ability to shape a model on the data of its own population, keep it under its own governance, regulate it according to its own values and context, and operate it through a health workforce with the capacity to evaluate its outputs. A ministry that cannot inspect a model, audit its performance against its own population's outcomes, or withdraw it from clinical use does not exercise meaningful oversight.Sovereignty in this context is not isolation; it is knowing where data sit, who processes them, under whose law, and on what terms access can be revoked. Without populationrepresentative data, locally grounded regulation, and a trained workforce able to question and override the system where necessary, the populations furthest behind will bear the greatest exposure to model failure, precisely because they are least represented in training data and least resourced to identify when a system is underperforming. This is a critical moment to set a shared direction for how AI in health is governed. documents.abstract: Human-AI Teams (HATs) are evolving into increasingly complex multi-human multi-agent structures, including those with hierarchical leadership and role accountability. Conventionally, humans have primarily taken leadership positions, directing and supervising autonomous agents. However, emerging HAT contexts now enable humans to assume a wider range of hierarchical roles within teams, including both leader and follower positions. Despite these developments, empirical research on non-dyadic HATs remains limited, leaving important questions regarding trust and teamwork in complex team structures largely unexplored. In this study, we investigate how hierarchical roles differentially shape trust in AI teammates and trust in the team as a whole, as well as how role-based trust divergence associates with overall team outcomes. We find that trust varies significantly by the trustor’s role, yet shared trust and reduced trust divergence across teammates are critical for better team performance. Accordingly, it is important to support shared team cognition and mitigate trust divergence.

Educational institutions are increasingly regarded as environments where regulatory expectations, quality development, safety awareness, and sustainability come together. This study investigates how the joint implementation of ISO 14001 (environmental management), ISO 9001 (quality management), and ISO 45001 (occupational health and safety) influences school culture, student behaviour, and stakeholder participation in different school settings in Düzce, Türkiye, including preschool, primary, lower secondary, and special education institutions. The Learning Integrated School Model (LISM) is introduced as a conceptual framework that interprets these standards as interconnected components of an organisational learning structure rather than separate technical requirements. The research was designed as a qualitative case study. Semi-structured interviews with 10 school administrators and 18 teachers were conducted through maximum variation sampling to reflect diverse implementation experiences. Interview data were analysed by thematic content analysis, and reliability was reinforced through dual coding, participant confirmation, and expert feedback. The findings suggest that integrated management systems contribute to environmentally aware and safety-oriented behavioural patterns among students and support more reflective planning and monitoring in instructional processes. They also encourage cooperation and shared ownership among staff, while sustainability-based behaviours extend the school’s influence into family environments. At the same time, documentation workload, time constraints, resource limitations, and differing levels of engagement present challenges that shape the continuity of these systems. It is concluded that the Learning Integrated School Model creates a continuous learning cycle by aligning environmental, quality, and safety practices, thereby reinforcing sustainability-oriented school culture. More effective digital documentation tools, expanded role-based professional development, and structured networks for sharing implementation experiences may strengthen integration efforts. The study offers a perspective that views integrated management systems as contributors to educational transformation, providing insights for both practitioners and policy development.

Background: Fresh graduates face an increasingly difficult school-to-work transition, while artificial intelligence (AI) has become a routine study and job-search companion; yet how the intention to use AI translates into employability, and through which mechanisms, remains unclear. Objective: Grounded in Social Cognitive Theory, this study tests whether behavioral intention to use AI is associated with self-perceived graduate employability directly and indirectly through career adaptability and job search self-efficacy, and whether AI self-efficacy and AI trust moderate these paths. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey of 612 Indonesian fresh graduates who use AI for career preparation was analyzed with partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Results: AI use intention positively predicted career adaptability (β = 0.305) and job search self-efficacy (β = 0.249), and both resources predicted self-perceived employability. The indirect paths through both resources were significant, and a direct effect of AI use intention on employability remained, indicating partial mediation. AI self-efficacy and AI trust showed significant main effects on their resources, while the interaction-related indirect effects were not significant. Conclusion: AI use intention is associated with self-perceived employability through career adaptability and job search self-efficacy. The cross-sectional findings do not establish causality. Educational institutions and career-service units may use these findings to inform structured AI-supported occupational exploration, skills-gap analysis, résumé refinement, and interview rehearsal, while encouraging critical verification of AI outputs.

This study examines linguistic and stylistic over-elaboration in beginner Arabic writing produced during a classroom task permitting generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and electronic translation. The study emerged from an Arabic language course involving undergraduate accounting students at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), Terengganu Branch, Malaysia. Students were instructed to write a simple birthday invitation addressed to friends, using accessible vocabulary and including specified invitation elements. During the review of approximately 100 submissions, the instructor observed recurring instances of vocabulary, courtesy expressions, and sentence formulations that appeared more sophisticated or formal than expected for the learners' proficiency and the task's communicative purpose. Adopting an exploratory qualitative approach, the study draws on these professional classroom observations, supplemented by the direct examination of three available invitation texts. The analysis considers lexical overreach, stylistic over-elaboration, unnecessary syntactic complexity, register mismatch, and learner-level appropriateness. The findings highlight a pedagogical distinction between linguistic correctness and the suitability of written expression for a beginner's level and communicative situation. They also suggest that apparently sophisticated writing should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of independent linguistic proficiency. Because individual tool use and writing processes were not documented, the study does not attribute particular expressions to GenAI or establish causal effects.

Abstract This paper deals with the technology of localization of pathological foci of radiopharmaceutical accumulation based on deep learning methods. It can be used in departments of radionuclide diagnostics (nuclear medicine) as a second opinion in the description of radionuclide studies by a radiologist, as well as a way of early diagnosis of tumors and metastatic lesions, assessment of the effectiveness of treatment, including differential diagnosis of the disease. The paper presents the results of computational experiment conducted with the trained model on test data. As a result, the model achieved an accuracy of 89% on the test sample.

documents.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the systemic tensions between traditional library values and rapid technological adoption in 2026. Design/methodology/approach The paper synthesizes findings from recent industry reports including Marshall Breeding’s, 2026 Library Systems Report and analysis of landmark legal cases on e-lending. Findings The central theme in 2026 is “Innovation under Constraint.” Libraries globally face austerity versus AI disruption, exploitative e-book licensing models, generative AI hallucinations, high-stakes cloud migration failures and the conflict between surveillance infrastructure and patron privacy. Originality/value The paper provides a critical practitioner perspective on how libraries are negotiating technological change while defending their role as democratic trust anchors.

documents.abstract: Abstract As AI agents start to act in European critical infrastructure (telecom networks, payment systems, cloud platforms and industrial robots), a recurring gap appears. A system can log that an operation was authorized and acknowledged, yet still be unable to show that the evidence behind it was current, or that the reported result matches what actually happened. This gap matters to obligations under the EU AI Act, including: risk management (Article 9); record-keeping and logging (Article 12); human oversight (Article 14); accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity (Article 15); post-market monitoring and serious-incident reporting (Articles 72–73). This publication presents the foundational part of a 15-part technical series, also submitted as an IETF Internet-Draft. It defines a vendor-neutral evidence-consistency framework built on these elements: every consequential operation receives a stable identity and a declared verification objective; each observation carries its provenance, resource generation, time interval and clock uncertainty; domain-specific checks produce a scoped three-valued result: SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED or UNRESOLVED. UNRESOLVED is a first-class outcome. Missing or stale evidence is recorded honestly rather than reported as success, which gives auditors, oversight personnel and incident investigators a reconstructable decision record. The framework keeps verification separate from authority. A positive result never grants permission to act; any consequential effect stays under a separate, accountable control boundary. Acknowledgement, completion, physical outcome and financial settlement are reconciled as independent evidence. A three-layer architecture keeps shared evidence semantics apart from twelve domain profiles: radio access and network incident recovery; telecom sessions and charging; hardware and DMA command paths; multi-agent negotiation and asynchronous tools; robotics and physical safety; multilingual emergency instructions; browser agents and agent migration; autonomous commerce; accelerator reset. The material is also relevant to engineering work under NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act, DORA and the Machinery Regulation. The PDF includes: a reader's summary with diagrams; an analytical latency and capacity model with a measurement plan; 12 proposed verification tests; threat and edge-case profiles; a searchable catalogue of 639 engineering mechanisms. The document describes technical mechanisms and makes no legal-compliance, certification or conformity claim.

documents.abstract: Chronic occupational exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) has been linked to an elevated risk of respiratory diseases, but the association between this exposure and the incidence of rare histological types of lung cancer has not yet been sufficiently studied. The current retrospective cohort study assesses the association between cumulative occupational exposure to PM2.5 and the incidence of rare lung cancer subtypes among industrial workers. Information on occupational health, occupational exposure measurements, and regional cancer registry data obtained in 2006-2023 have been used for the analysis. This study covers 6,500 employees of mining, construction, and metalworking industries. Exposures of individuals were determined from PM₂.₅ measurements in the workplace and the use of job-exposure matrices. Rare lung cancer events were documented from histopathology reports and categorized based on standardized tumor classification. Over a median follow-up of 13.4 years, 226 lung cancer events were documented, with 39 rare histology types (17.3%). The highest PM₂.₅ exposure group had an increased risk of rare lung cancer compared to the lowest PM₂.₅ exposure group (HR = 1.79; 95%CI: 1.18–2.71; p = 0.004). From the continuous exposure model, there was increased risk for each 10 µg/m³ increase in cumulative exposure to PM₂.₅. It can be concluded that long-term exposure to PM₂.₅ at workplaces increases the incidence of rare lung cancer subtypes.

documents.abstract: Introduction Generative AI weakens the correspondence between the final text of an assignment and the argumentative work involved in producing it. This study examined how task structure and AI-use instructions shape evidence use, engagement with objections, and revision in university ideological and political education. Methods An LLM simulation crossed three task formats—position essays, evidence-integration memoranda, and follow-up-and-revision defense tasks—with three AI-use scenarios—simulated no-AI, responsible collaboration, and concealed ghostwriting. Two raters coded 148 generated texts with the Textual Response Artifact Scoring Index (TRASI), and an anonymous questionnaire collected 268 evaluations of 27 selected texts. Results Responsible collaboration produced the highest overall rubric score ( M = 3.32). Evidence-integration memoranda ( M = 3.16) and follow-up-and-revision defenses ( M = 3.10) exceeded position essays ( M = 2.63). Position essays varied most across the three AI-use scenarios, whereas the memorandum and defense showed narrower differences because their instructions already required source explanation or response and revision. Questionnaire participants distinguished the same task functions: memoranda were rated highest for source–claim linkage, and defenses for counterargument response and revision explanation. Open-ended responses associated evidence integration, comparison of reasons, and revision with thinking, while formulaic structure, over-polished expression, and generic abstraction were associated with AI-like writing. Discussion Task structure and AI-use instructions were functionally complementary. Structured tasks elicited source explanation or challenge and revision directly, so responsible collaboration added its largest contribution in the general position essay. GenAI-mediated assessment can therefore be designed around the argumentative decisions that writers are required to document.

Background Despite the substantial growth of research on Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) in higher education, the field remains characterized by geographic concentration, methodological constraints, and conceptual fragmentation between established competence frameworks and emerging demands such as climate literacy and green skills. No prior review has simultaneously mapped the bibliometric architecture and conducted an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted inductive thematic synthesis of this domain. Methods A dual-method design integrated bibliometric network analysis—co-citation, bibliographic coupling, and keyword co-occurrence—with AI-assisted inductive thematic synthesis. A total of 442 peer-reviewed documents were retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and ERIC (2015–2026) through systematic multi-database search, deduplication, and PICO-adapted relevance screening evaluated by a specialized multi-rater panel (Fleiss’ κ=0.55 – 0.69 , 98.4% unanimous agreement on the retained corpus). Thematic extraction was performed using two complementary large language model architectures (Qwen3-235B and DeepSeek V3.2), governed by a stringent verification protocol achieving a 92.0% alignment score; 37 hallucination flags were audited and corrected via human expert review. Results The corpus exhibits substantial and accelerated scientific expansion since 2019 ( R2=0.91 for exponential fit; compound annual growth rate of 18.4%), with Spain, the United Kingdom, and Germany accounting for over one-third of output. Five thematic clusters emerged: curriculum integration, transformative pedagogies, institutional and faculty roles, sustainability literacy and behavioral outcomes, and digital innovation. Surveys and case studies dominate research designs (37.7%), while experimental approaches represent only 4.0% of the corpus. Green skills and climate literacy remain conceptually peripheral despite their policy urgency, institutional collaboration is fragmented (20.3% of institutions isolated), and faculty populations are understudied (7.0%) relative to students (32.7%). Fifty-six knowledge gaps were identified across structural, declared, and emergent categories, with methods-by-concepts coverage reaching 64.0%. Conclusions The field would benefit from a methodological transition toward longitudinal and experimental designs, enhanced visibility of Global South scholarship (contextualizing database indexing constraints), systematic pedagogical theorization of simulation-based approaches, and deliberate cross-institutional consortia to transition from conceptual proliferation to evidence-based pedagogical science.

Ergonomic challenges in university learning environments are increasingly recognized as important factors influencing student health and academic performance.However, there is limited evidence on how these challenges interact with socio-demographic factors such as marital status, particularly in low-and middle-income countries.This cross-sectional study was conducted among 352 students at the University of Calabar, Nigeria.Data were collected using a structured online questionnaire that incorporated elements of the Standard Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire.Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and logistic regression were applied to examine the relationship between marital status, cumulative ergonomic challenges, and academic performance.Married students accounted for 2.56% of the study population.Commonly reported ergonomic challenges included musculoskeletal strain, poor lighting, non-adjustable furniture, and inadequate learning infrastructure.A moderate positive relationship was observed between cumulative ergonomic burden and academic performance impairment (r = 0.508), although this was not statistically significant.In the unadjusted analysis, married female students had higher exposure to ergonomic stressors and poorer academic outcomes compared to their male counterparts (OR = 2.00).However, after adjusting for ergonomic burden, this relationship reversed (AOR = 0.533), suggesting that the observed differences were largely driven by unequal exposure to environmental stressors rather than gender.Ergonomic challenges are a significant but often overlooked determinant of academic performance among university students.These findings highlight the need for institution-wide ergonomic interventions, particularly for vulnerable groups, to improve learning conditions, reduce physical strain, and support better academic outcomes.

Digital media constitute relevant spaces for the socialization of masculinities, where gender norms, belonging, vulnerability, and hostility may be reproduced, negotiated, or contested. This scoping review aimed to map the contributions, strategies, and possibilities of media literacy for recognizing, problematizing, and preventing online hostility related to the construction of masculinities among adolescents and young people in educational contexts. The review followed Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and the PRISMA-ScR framework. Fifty-three articles published between 2021 and 2026 were included, identified through SciELO, the Virtual Health Library, and the CAPES Journals Portal; data were extracted using a standardized matrix and synthesized descriptively and thematically. The synthesis resulted in five axes: digital masculinities; education, intervention, and prevention; hostile communities and radicalization; vulnerability, belonging, and recognition; and online hostility and masculine norms. Media literacy was explicitly addressed in nine studies and involved gender perspectives, critical analysis of influencers, gender disinformation, algorithmic awareness, consent, empathy, and peer support. Only two interventions were evaluated. Preventive strategies should therefore integrate masculine socialization, belonging, vulnerability, and sociotechnical mediation, while further intervention, longitudinal, and youth-centered studies are needed.

This exploration examines the impact of supplementary AI-generated explanatory materials on foundational mathematics learning and creative metacognition in primary education. The study followed a quantitative, quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design with a nonequivalent control group. Fourth-grade classes in five schools were assigned to conditions at the classroom level: an intervention group receiving AI-facilitated handouts (n = 135) and a control group using programmatic textbooks (n = 128). Students in the experimental condition received eight supplementary lessons featuring paper-based handouts. These handouts presented explanations, examples, and illustrations of new mathematical topics generated by a large language model (Gemini 2.5 Pro), prompted the inclusion of age-appropriate content and a dedicated section encouraging creative metacognition (reflection and novel idea generation). Baseline equivalence was confirmed. The outcomes assessed included single-digit mental arithmetic, multidigit calculation, arithmetic word problem-solving, and creative metacognition, which were analyzed via multilevel or robust linear modeling accounting for classroom clustering. The results indicated no statistically significant differences between groups on single-digit mental arithmetic tasks. However, students who received AI-generated materials showed significantly greater improvement in multidigit calculation tasks and one-step word problem-solving than did the control group. No significant difference was found for multistep word problems. The intervention group also presented a substantially greater increase in creative metacognition scores than did the control group. The findings provide preliminary quasi-experimental evidence that curated, static AI-generated explanations, when designed to include metacognitive prompts, may be associated with greater gains in specific procedural and applied mathematical skills and creative metacognition among fourth-grade students under the conditions studied. This approach illustrates how generative AI can be leveraged as an authoring tool to supplement standard instruction and cultivate higher-order cognitive skills in young learners.

Evaluation of medical AI has inherited its instruments from the evaluation of people: examinations, expert judgement of free text, and task value denominated in the hours a practitioner would need. This working paper asks which of those instruments survive when the thing measured is a silicon producer (a model running inside a harness with tools) and builds a measurement framework for the parts that do not. It is the argument for the construction of the MedGauge Methodology, version 0.1.0 (https://medgauge.org/methodology/text/), which is the normative text. It tests the claim that silicon producers differ from human producers against the literature and finds twelve properties of silicon producers that bear on measurement, each stated with its counter-evidence; a difference from people is supported for two of them by an opened source, three hold by construction of the subject, and for the remaining seven no source states the human side and no difference is asserted. It shows that human-anchored evaluations divide into anchors on human time (which transfer as a predictor of difficulty but not as a unit), on a human product or rule (which transfer once the product is converted into a key of field checks set independently by two experts) and on human judgement of free text or preference (which do not transfer). On that basis it builds the measurement: following the international vocabulary of metrology, the reference of each quantity moves from a unit to a versioned grading program applied to a fixed artifact contract. It gives scale rules for labels, levels and counts; proposes base and derived quantities with their scale type, traceability and cross-harness comparability; maps them onto ten measurement dimensions and ten task labels; and sets out an examination regime in which a subject passes only if every task passes in all three runs with no safety veto, the strength of a pass being a one-sided 95% lower bound on reliability, with execution errors counted as failures, paired comparison with step-down multiplicity control, and no overall score. Version 0.1.0 of the methodology sets no level threshold and issues no level. The paper proposes a four-layer task typology with its literature base, explains why a closed, uncalibrated, generated task set licenses an attribute-sampling regime but not a response-model regime, and sets out the uncertainty budget for the chain from a published score to its public source clause. Standardised semantics for products, scenarios and task types, and the validation of those standards, are set out as a research plan, not as results. The paper reports no measurement result. At the date of publication the public site is live, no benchmark round has been run, no result record exists and every leaderboard is empty.

documents.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence is profoundly reshaping the relationship between knowledge, education, and society, prompting pedagogy to reconsider the ways teaching and learning are understood. The educational challenge extends beyond the introduction of innovative technologies into schools and concerns the processes through which knowledge is produced, interpreted, or ganized, and shared. As highlighted by UNESCO (2023), artificial intelligence represents one of the major educational challenges of our time because it actively influences the construction of meaning and transforms the forms of cultural mediation traditionally performed by schools. Consequently, the central issue is not whether AI should be embraced or rejected, but how it can be integrated into pedagogical practices that foster critical thinking and digital citizenship. The evolution of digital environments demonstrates that access to information no longer guarantees knowledge construction. Chapter in: Francesco Peluso Cassese (ed.), Algorithmic Heartbeats: Affective Education in the Age of the Fourth Revolution, REN Press – Cares srl, 2026, pp. 343-344. ISBN 979-12-82860-00-0. Volume DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23211262. Section: Teacher Education Between the "Frankenstein Complex" and the D-Generation.

In 2024, revision of the Enforcement Decree of the Higher Education Act in Korea abolished the rigid division between the 2-year premedical phase and the 4-year medical phase, allowing medical schools to design 6-year curricula autonomously for the first time in a century. Universities nationwide have begun redesigning their programs accordingly. This historic reform coincides with the rapid spread of generative artificial intelligence (AI) across society, including the ways students learn. In the current curriculum reform discourse, however, AI is discussed almost exclusively as content to be taught or as a supplementary tool to be used, whereas the more fundamental question of AI as an educational agent remains largely unexamined. Outside the formal curriculum, AI tutors already function as de facto teachers: a randomized experiment suggests that well-designed AI tutoring can outperform expert- led active-learning classrooms, and international surveys indicate that medical students routinely consult AI before, or instead of, their professors. This paper argues that the widening gap between the official, faculty-centered curriculum and the actual AI-mediated learning ecosystem may create discord: AI-mediated learning may become an unmanaged informal curriculum, faculty-designed assessment may lose authority, and trust in the formal curriculum may erode. Curriculum reform that merely rearranges the 6-year structure without addressing who teaches risks producing an elaborate design for an education that no longer reflects how learning occurs. Medical schools should explicitly define the position, scope, and governance of AI as an educational agent within their new curricula.

documents.abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid population aging and the proliferation of Large Language Models (LLMs) in China, this study investigates the dynamics of trust formation and adjustment among Chinese older adults during their initial encounters with LLM agents. Through in-depth interviews conducted before, during, and immediately after 30 older adults’ first interactions with six widely used Chinese LLM applications, followed by second interviews with 26 participants, the study examines how trust was initially formed and adjusted over the short term. Findings reveal that pre-interaction responses were predominantly characterized by low interest and skepticism, rooted in sociocultural perceptions rather than just technological barriers. Analysis identified four technological factors associated with participants’ trust-related judgments during engagement, including personalization, anthropomorphism, conversationality, and response latency. Longitudinal analysis identified three behavioral patterns of trust adjustment: Limited Correction, Collaborative Reciprocity, and Cognitive Entrenchment. These findings advance theoretical understanding of trust adjustment and calibration-related processes and offer design implications for building more trustworthy LLMs.

This study examines the theological significance of the doctrine of Imago Dei in response to the ethical challenges posed by artificial intelligence to human dignity and identity. Utilizing a qualitative literature review approach, the research analyzes how technological advancements in AI necessitate a profound reflection on theological anthropology. The findings indicate that the Imago Dei remains the foundational framework for affirming human uniqueness and dignity amidst digital progress. Consequently, AI development and utilization must be guided by Christian ethical principles to ensure technology supports human well-being without eroding core values. Ultimately, the study highlights the need for a contextual reconstruction of Christian spirituality and ethics, enabling believers to engage with AI wisely, responsibly, and in alignment with their divine calling as God's image.

documents.abstract: Memory-OS is an AI-powered Personal Knowledge Operating System designed to unify personal and development-related information through a conversational command-line interface. The system integrates external knowledge sources such as GitHub, Gmail, and Notion through a connector-based architecture and processes collected information for efficient retrieval. It uses a local sentence-transformer model to generate embeddings, Qdrant for vector storage, Neo4j for knowledge graph relationships, and SQLite for structured data management. A hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline combines semantic search, keyword-based retrieval, and graph-based context to generate relevant and context-aware responses using a Groq-powered Large Language Model (LLM). Memory-OS also provides an interactive terminal interface, a full-screen Textual TUI, workspace management, incremental synchronization, Docker-based service provisioning, health diagnostics, backup and restore functionality, and performance monitoring. The primary objective is to reduce information fragmentation by enabling users to search, connect, and understand their accumulated knowledge through natural-language queries instead of manually navigating multiple applications.

documents.abstract: This contribution analyses the relationship between mirror neurons, Artificial Intelligence, Affective Computing, and educational technologies for the socio-emotional inclusion of students with ASD. Social robots, augmented reality, and intelligent systems are understood as pedagogical mediators, capable of making social cues more accessible and fostering personalised learning environments. The mirror neuron system offers a key framework for understanding the embodied nature of intersubjectivity. The sharing of neural codes between observed and executed actions allows imitation, empathy, and the understanding of others to be interpreted as processes integrating perception, action, and emotion (Gallese, 2008). Learning is thus a relational, situated experience. This framework dialogues with AI architectures. Artificial neural networks learn from data and generalise responses, but their pedagogical value depends on supporting adaptive interactions. Social robots, immersive environments, and augmented reality may offer structured contexts in which students exercise communicative and socio-emotional skills through feedback and recognisable routines. Chapter in: Francesco Peluso Cassese (ed.), Algorithmic Heartbeats: Affective Education in the Age of the Fourth Revolution, REN Press – Cares srl, 2026, pp. 47-48. ISBN 979-12-82860-00-0. Volume DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23211262. Section: Social Robotics and Socio-Emotional Inclusion.

In the face of growing consumer demands, tightening legal regulations, and the global problem of food waste, the meat industry is undergoing a dynamic transformation. Traditional, synthetic additive-based preservation methods are being replaced by innovative, integrated technologies. This review article analyzes the latest scientific reports (from 2016–2026) indexed in Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect databases regarding modern methods of meat and meat product preservation. The mechanisms of action and the impact of advanced non-thermal technologies, such as high hydrostatic pressure (HPP), high-intensity ultrasound (HIU), atmospheric pressure cold plasma (ACP), pulsed light (PL), and rotating and oscillating magnetic fields (RMF/OMF), are discussed in detail. The role of biopreservation in the context of the “clean label” trend was also presented, including the use of lactic acid bacteria, bacteriocins, bacteriophages, and nanoencapsulated plant extracts. Furthermore, innovations in materials engineering were analyzed—active packaging releasing antimicrobial substances and intelligent freshness indicators based on natural halochrome dyes. The whole is complemented by an analysis of the impact of Industry 4.0 solutions, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), hyperspectral imaging (HSI), and the Internet of Things (IoT), on cold chain optimization and digital quality management.

Introduction. The modernization of monitoring procedures is recognized as critical to improving the objectivity and effectiveness of rehabilitation interventions in the physical education of students with disabilities. The purpose of the study was to develop and conduct experimental and metrological testing of smart electronic system for monitoring the rehabilitation process of students with disabilities following blast-induced traumatic brain injury. Materials and Methods. The study was conducted in three consecutive stages: theoretical justification; the development of a smart electronic system pedagogical experiment and data processing using mathematical statistics methods. The study involved first-year students (28 males) with disabilities following a blast traumatic brain injury, who were enrolled in a physical education course lasting one academic semester. The Push & Release Test was used to collect empirical data. Results. The study aims to develop an intelligent electronic system for the objective monitoring of the P&R Test, particularly those parameters that cannot be recorded visually. An intelligent electronic system has been developed and tested, consisting of a sensor module (a smart IMU sensor based on a microcontroller, accelerometer, gyroscope, and magnetometer), an impact force and alignment measurement module (a strain gauge platform with four high-precision strain sensors), an intelligent data processing unit with an Arduino microcontroller, and a personal computer with real-time wireless signal transmission. The system’s functional components were modeled in Python using artificial intelligence algorithms to automate the analysis and prediction of students’ functional status from test results. The implementation of neural network-based artificial intelligence algorithms enabled the automatic classification of movement patterns and the highly accurate prediction of students’ functional status following a mild traumatic brain injury. A virtual reality interface is integrated into the system, creating a «virtual mirror» effect for interactive feedback. Empirical and metrological validation of the system confirmed its high reliability (ICC – 0.844) and validity (ICC – 0.521) compared to traditional expert assessment reliability (ICC – 0.506) and validity (ICC – 0.188) by an examiner. Conclusions. The developed digital system provides examiners with qualitative and quantitative data, minimizes the «human factor», and significantly improves the effectiveness of monitoring the rehabilitation process of students with blast TBI during a university physical education course.

The growing prevalence of digital technologies and the increasing linguistic diversity of contemporary societies are profoundly changing the processes of language teaching and learning (Piccardo, 2019). Against this backdrop, multilingualism and multisensory technologies represent two closely interlinked dimensions, capable of contributing to the creation of educational environments that are more inclusive, participatory and geared towards the development of language skills (Kress, 2021). This paper presents a review of the international literature with the aim of analysing the relationship between multilingualism and digital technologies, with particular reference to immersive environments, artificial intelligence systems and Digital Language Learning Ecosystems (PintoLlorente & Alvarez, 2024). The analysis takes into account theoretical studies, meta -analyses and systematic reviews published in recent years, linking the main findings of research on language learning with the latest technological innovations. Chapter in: Francesco Peluso Cassese (ed.), Algorithmic Heartbeats: Affective Education in the Age of the Fourth Revolution, REN Press – Cares srl, 2026, pp. 153-155. ISBN 979-12-82860-00-0. Volume DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23211262. Section: Hybrid and "Emotionally Aware" Learning Environments.

Cross-border health-care information systems often struggle to deliver culturally embedded medical knowledge—such as traditional Chinese medicine—to international users with varying health literacy, due to fragmented architecture and weak semantic alignment across languages. This study proposed a tripartite framework built on the Qwen2.5 Vision-Language model at the 7-billion parameter scale, integrating cross-lingual perception, domain knowledge enhancement, and terminology alignment to support multimodal health-care information processing. A bidirectional label-matching feedback mechanism and an entropy-weighted coupling coordination model were developed to quantify system-level synergy. Using 12,642 dissemination records and 7,869 health-care cases (2019–2025), the proposed system outperformed OpenAI's generative pretrained transformer 4o mini by 7.1 points on average across core indicators, with coupling coordination rising from 0.409 to 0.716 and regional synergy gains of 0.382 in Southeast Asia. The framework achieved a 39.2% retention rate in full-chain service conversion and over 83% adaptability for low-health-literacy users.

documents.abstract: Musculoskeletal neck pain (NP) is more common in people with headaches (HA) than in those without HA. NP is most frequently associated with primary forms of HA. In real-world clinical practice, patients with NP and concomitant HA are often misdiagnosed, with HA being regarded as secondary and associated with organic pathology of the cervical spine. Consequently, such patients often do not receive effective treatment, or the treatment provided has only a temporary effect. We present the case of a female patient with migraine and NP. A combined approach was used to treat the patient, comprising a course of a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (Nimesil) and non-pharmacological therapy – educational discussions with the patient about the condition, individual kinesiotherapy sessions, kinesiotaping, training in ergonomic principles and correct posture, and physical activity in daily life. After 2 months of treatment, the patient’s musculoskeletal pain and headaches associated with cervical myofascial pain syndrome had resolved; only rare migraine attacks remained, which were effectively relieved by a triptan. Follow-up of the patient over a 12-month period demonstrated the sustainability of the clinical improvement achieved, confirming the effectiveness of the described therapeutic approach in the treatment of musculoskeletal neck pain and associated migraine.

Background/Objectives: Time spent in unchanging environments is associated with poorer brain, cognitive and mental health outcomes, while environmental enrichment for humans is measured by how much nature is present rather than how it changes. Methods: This study quantified nature’s changing visual complexity using a large-language-model scoring method validated against a deep-learning complexity metric previously tested using event-related potentials. Photos were taken of a natural scene, a tree, and the sky across minutes, days, and seasons (1115 photographs; 2024 to 2026). Results: The analysis identified seven quantitative properties describing nature’s dynamic environmental enrichment in changing visual complexity: Dichotomy, Inclination, Unpredictability, Renewal, Net balance, Amplitude, and Level (DIURNAL). A quantitative simulation then showed that a natural view offers more change than indoor and urban views, consistent with the argument that unchanging environments are detrimental to the brain, which is hypothesised here to act through a dopaminergic pathway. Conclusions: DIURNAL raises questions for biophilic design and for how neurotypical and neurodivergent brains respond to change in visual complexity in nature, digital environments and built environments.

This study quantified nature’s changing visual complexity using a large-language-model scoring method validated against a deep-learning complexity metric previously tested using event-related potentials. Photos were taken of a natural scene, a tree, and the sky across minutes, days, and seasons (1,115 photographs; 2024 to 2026). The analysis identified seven quantitative properties describing nature’s dynamic environmental enrichment in changing visual complexity: Dichotomy, Inclination, Unpredictability, Renewal, Net balance, Amplitude, and Level (DIURNAL). A quantitative simulation then showed that a natural view offers more change than indoor and urban views, consistent with the argument that unchanging environments are detrimental to the brain, hypothesised here to act through a dopaminergic pathway. Office workers are at risk of developing neck pain (NP), which is one of the main causes of temporary incapacity for work and disability. NP associated with office work is caused by a combination of individual, physical and psychosocial factors. Identifying the factors that predispose office workers to the development and chronicity of NP may contribute to the primary and secondary prevention of pain. A multisystem approach to the treatment and prevention of NP among office workers is recognized as the most effective; it includes optimization of the work-place in accordance with ergonomic principles, therapeutic exercises and psychological intervention. The drugs of choice for relieving NP are nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, among which aceclofenac (Aertal) is one of the most effective and safe.

Introduction Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers significant opportunities to improve healthcare quality, especially in critical care settings, where timely decisions are essential yet challenging due to the volume of continuously accumulating patient data. AI algorithms can analyze data in real time, summarize key information for busy care teams, and alert clinicians to critical events and important care milestones. However, successful implementation requires first understanding the needs and barriers care teams face, including needs that are currently missing from their workflow, and what obstacles to integration exist. Methods To address these questions, we conducted a field study in a Cardiothoracic Intensive Care Unit (CT-ICU) to evaluate user needs for implementing real-time AI predictive analytics. We observed and interviewed fourteen participants ( n = 14), including nursing staff, advanced practice providers (NP/PAs), cardiovascular critical care attending physicians, and surgeons. Through a qualitative thematic analysis, we identified key considerations for developing and implementing static and real-time AI and predictive tools in the CT-ICU, aligning with the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) constructs of perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use . Findings Key themes included: (1) the system must have added clinical value to the clinical team and patients, (2) trust in the AI system should be prioritized through co-design processes, transparency in the system, and consistent prediction accuracy, and (3) integration into workflow was critical, including robust onboarding and minimizing alarm fatigue, charting burden, click burden, and technology burden with consideration of personal wellness. Conclusion As a synthesis of our findings, we identify a series of key design insights and suggest a preliminary framework for AI technology development focused on clinical team trust and adoption, the Trusted AI for Clinical Teams (TACT) framework. These findings offer the potential to bridge from AI research to clinical implementation.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Aims Healthcare workers (HCWs) are frequently exposed to psychosocial job demands (JDs) that may lead to work-related stress. This study investigates the association between JDs—specifically time pressure, problem solving, overload, and emotional demands—and hair cortisol concentration (HCC), as biomarker of long-term hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis activation, in a sample of HCWs. It further examines the moderating role of negative affectivity (NA), an individual characteristic linked to heightened stress reactivity. Drawing on the Job Demands–Resources theory and the allostatic load model, we hypothesized that (1) JDs would be positively associated with HCC and (2) this relationship would be stronger for individuals high in NA. Design Participants were 67 healthcare professionals working in a healthcare facility located in Northern Italy. Participants completed a self-report questionnaire designed to assess JDs and NA. Next, participants provided a hair sample for the assessment of HCC. Results Although data from a sample of HCWs revealed some positive but non-significant trends for problem solving and overload, generally JDs were not associated with HCC at average levels of NA. Interestingly, NA moderated the relationship between problem solving/time pressure and HCC, with stronger positive associations among individuals with high NA. Conclusion Findings from this exploratory cross-sectional study suggest that NA may act as a vulnerability factor, implying that HCWs high in NA may have a heightened strain response to certain JDs. By integrating psychological and biological measures, this study offers novel insights into the interplay between workplace stressors, personality traits, and physiological responses to stress. These findings highlight the potential relevance of individual differences in occupational stress research, and point to HCC as a promising indicator of chronic stress among HCWs. Implications for the profession The findings suggest the need for occupational health interventions tailored to individual traits, such as NA, to reduce stress reactivity, foster well-being, and enhance the quality of care provided.

Purpose Periodic risk reports constitute a substantial repository of operational data for project management. Despite the inherent informational value, archived records remain largely unstructured and highly fragmented. This study proposes a fully local neuro-symbolic approach for dynamic risk forecasting by translating qualitative project narratives into a quantifiable predictive engine to support decision-making. Design/methodology/approach The proposed methodology adopts a mixed-methods architecture including four layers: (1) spatial morphology reconstruction using a Y-axis density clustering algorithm; (2) a hybrid pseudonymization filter; (3) a local large language model (LLM) with chain-of-thought reasoning; and (4) a symbolic causal engine powered by a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) to quantify causal propagation into a dynamic risk index. Findings An empirical evaluation across 28 reporting cycles spanning a 33-month large-scale infrastructure project indicates that the symbolic layer provides a temporally coherent aggregation of the output of a zero-shot perception layer operating at a macro F1-score of 53.62%. By quantifying causal risk propagation, the DBN captured a 93.59% risk-saturation state, for which the retrieved evidence identifies chronic site-clearance bottlenecks. Notably, using an alert threshold selected by sensitivity analysis together with an analytic constraint on the posterior mass attributable to the critical state (talert = 70.0%), the model outputs Bayesian probabilities alongside LLM-extracted textual evidence, yielding an anticipation interval of 1.33 reporting cycles relative to the documented administrative response. Originality/value The neuro-symbolic framework bridges the gap between deep learning perception and causal inference in construction management. By coupling LLM-driven zero-shot ordinal extraction with DBN causal reasoning, the research establishes an auditable framework for risk documentation. The integrated framework transitions AI from an opaque prediction model into an accountable decision-support tool, providing stakeholders with transparent explainable AI diagnostics and supporting a shift from reactive mitigation to proactive, evidence-based risk prevention.

School dropout is a major dare for Moroccan education systems. It generates profound repercussions, both socially and economically, affecting both individuals and the entire community. To assess the risks associated with this phenomenon, it is essential to use innovative technologies, relying in particular on statistical methods and artificial intelligence models capable of providing effective results using available data. These methods offer the possibility of identifying the factors influencing the educational phenomenon and anticipating the associated risks. To understand the effect of scholars’ social, economic, and personal influences on school dropout, we propose in this work a new classifier, based on an improvement of support vector machines (SVM) and on the ABC algorithm. We also present a regression model designed to estimate academic performance based on the average grade obtained. We also propose a new regression model to predict the degree of academic achievement. The proposed model was validated on a real dataset, compiled from a questionnaire distributed to Moroccan secondary school students. Furthermore, several comparative studies were conducted with recent approaches to assess the performance of the proposed methods. All the experimental results confirm the robustness and improved performance of the developed methods, particularly with respect to accuracy and predictive capability.
topics: Data Mining and Machine Learning Applications

documents.abstract: Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Big Data, academic libraries are evolving from traditional repositories into state-of-the-art, user-centric knowledge and research hubs. This chapter highlights key applications of AI and Big Data in academic libraries and explores the conceptual evolution of library services from Library 1.0 to Library 4.0. Technologies such as chatbots and virtual reference services, personalised recommendations, automated cataloguing and metadata generation, intelligent search capabilities, and research and learning analytics are all enabled by AI. Through Big Data analytics, libraries can better understand user behaviour, enhance collection development, maximise resource utilisation, and facilitate datadriven and predictive decision-making. Emerging technologies like blockchain, cloud computing, robotics, and the Internet of Things further support the development of smart library infrastructure. In India, technology-enabled library services are being facilitated by initiatives such as the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the National Digital Library of India (NDLI), e-ShodhSindhu, and Shodhganga. However, challenges such as data privacy, security, ethical bias, copyright issues, infrastructure, costs, interoperability, and a shortage of skilled personnel remain significant concerns. This chapter highlights the need for curriculum reform in Library and Information Science (LIS), emphasising areas such as artificial intelligence knowledge, data analytics, digital curation, user experience design, computer programming fundamentals, and continuous professional development. It concludes that ethical practices, ongoing training, and collaboration among librarians, technologists, educators, and policymakers can facilitate the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence and big data, thereby enhancing teaching, learning, research, and innovation in higher education.

Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a multifactorial clinical syndrome associated with rapid deterioration of renal function and involves interconnected processes including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, endothelial injury, programmed cell death, immune dysregulation and maladaptive repair. Current management is predominantly supportive and lacks effective pharmacological strategies that simultaneously address these pathological mechanisms. Renal-targeting nanozymes have emerged as promising catalytic nanotherapeutics that combine enzyme-mimicking activity with the tunable properties of nanomaterials. This review critically examines the engineering and therapeutic potential of renal-targeting nanozymes for AKI, focusing on nanozyme platforms, catalytic properties, renal-targeting strategies, and mechanisms underlying their antioxidant,immunomodulatory, cytoprotective, and regenerative effects. Preclinical evidence from experimental AKI models is discussed with emphasis on therapeutic outcomes, comparative performance, and current limitations. Particular attention is given to challenges involving renal accumulation, biodistribution, long-term biosafety, biodegradability,reproducibility, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory requirements. Emerging strategies, including biomimetic and biodegradable nanozymes, stimulus-responsive systems, theranostic platforms, and artificial intelligence-assisted nanozyme design, are also considered. Overall, renal-targeting nanozymes represent a promising multifunctional approach for addressing the complex pathophysiology of AKI. However, standardized preclinical evaluation, scalable manufacturing, comprehensive safety assessment, appropriate regulatory frameworks, and well-designed clinical studies remain essential for translating these catalytic nanotherapeutics into clinically viable precision therapies.

Sacrificial-anode cathodic protection remains one of the most widely applied corrosion mitigation strategies for metallic structures exposed to marine, freshwater, soil and industrial environments. Conventional zinc-, aluminum- and magnesium-based anodes have demonstrated long-standing practical value; however, increasing demands for extended service life, predictable electrochemical performance, environmental compliance and digital monitoring are reshaping the design criteria of modern cathodic protection systems. Recent research has therefore shifted from empirical alloy selection toward microstructure-controlled alloy design, smart sensing integration, data-driven prediction and sustainability-oriented material development. This critical review examines the evolution of sacrificial-anode technologies from conventional alloy systems to next-generation multifunctional anodes. Particular emphasis is placed on the relationship between alloy composition, microstructure, phase distribution, manufacturing route and electrochemical performance. The review further evaluates emerging smart sacrificial anodes incorporating embedded sensors, wireless monitoring and structural health monitoring functions, as well as the growing role of artificial intelligence, machine learning, digital twins and numerical simulation in corrosion prediction and anode lifetime assessment. Sustainability aspects, including lifecycle assessment, carbon footprint, recyclability, regulatory pressure and critical raw material dependency, are also critically discussed. This review differs from conventional alloy- or application-centered summaries by applying a four-part assessment structure: composition–processing–microstructure relationships; electrochemical and service-environment validation; sensing and data-driven lifetime management; and lifecycle sustainability. The structure is used to compare evidence maturity, identify application-specific failure modes and translate research gaps into qualification priorities. Current challenges include the lack of standardized performance datasets, limited long-term field validation, inconsistent correlation between laboratory and service environments, and insufficient integration of environmental metrics into anode design. Future research should focus on data-rich alloy development, sensor-enabled anode systems, predictive lifetime models and sustainable material selection strategies. The review concludes that next-generation sacrificial anodes will increasingly be defined not only by electrochemical efficiency, but also by intelligence, durability, environmental responsibility and system-level reliability.

Abstract Background Ensuring quality and safety of olive products is critical for consumer health, market value, and cultural heritage. Traditional destructive techniques are limited by their time-consuming and sample damage. Nondestructive techniques (NDT) allow real-time and non-invasive evaluation of authenticity, contamination, ripeness, and chemical composition. Artificial intelligence (AI) and big data analytics (BDA) integration enhances data interpretation, decision-making, and predictive modeling fostering transformative impact on olive industry. Aims This systematic review aimed to comprehensively evaluate advances in NDT for quality and safety assessment of olive products, emphasizing the role of AI and BDA and highlighting future prospects for industrial applications. Methods Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, from 2010 to 2026 involving spectroscopic, imaging, sensor-based methods, integrated with AI and BDA. Results NDT like near-infrared and Raman spectroscopy, ultrasound, hyperspectral and X-ray imaging, and electronic nose/tongue enable rapid and accurate assessment of chemical composition, contamination, and ripeness. When coupled with AI algorithms, they significantly improve detection sensitivity, classification accuracy, and real-time monitoring. BDA facilitate comprehensive data management, predictive modeling, and supply chain traceability. Computational pharmacology contributes to understanding complex chemical interactions and bioactive compound behavior in olive products, enhancing safety and quality assessments. Challenges include data heterogeneity, lack of standardization, high instrumentation costs, interpretability of AI models, and regulatory hurdles. Conclusion Integrating NDT with AI, BDA, and computational pharmacology offers a sustainable, efficient industrial pathway, with future research needed for standardization, portable device development, multi-sensor data fusion, and regulatory validation.

Methods for improving the safety of nuclear energy production and use facilities, including nuclear power plants (NPP) and other large industrial facilities in various countries, are presented and discussed. According to Concern «Rosenergoatom» data, the operation of all 10 Russian nuclear power plants (NPPs) was analyzed in details. The risks to the population in the region of each NPP were assessed when new reactors are commissioned under the Federal Purposed Program (FPP) forthe intensive development of the Russian nuclear energy industry until 2021. It was determined that all of them comply with permissible sanitary standards. Their background radiation levels do not exceed natural one. Measures were proposed to reduce the likelihood of uncontrolled chaos, strengthen favorable social dynamics and the human factor in preventing both natural and man-made disasters. In the context of the rapidly changing global political situation, several possible methods of protection against targeted terrorist attacks and unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) used for these purposes. This is a retrospective registration. The searches, screening, data extraction and synthesis described here were completed before this registration was submitted; the protocol was written in advance and held by the research team but was not publicly registered at the time. We are registering now to make the protocol and the a-priori decision rules publicly auditable. Objective: to map the published evidence on large language model (LLM) interventions that support health self-management among community-dwelling older adults, and to code, for every included report, the depth of nurse involvement using a six-level nurse-in-the-loop axis. Design: scoping review reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR and conducted following JBI methodology. Two reviewers screened and extracted independently in three consecutive batches (n = 40, 40, 27); disagreements were resolved against verbatim source text. Findings were synthesised descriptively as counts, proportions, a characteristics table and an evidence map; no meta-analysis and no weighting by quality.

documents.abstract: BACKGROUND: Disaster risk is increasing globally, placing growing pressure on health systems. In geographically isolated territories, seismovolcanic crises rapidly disrupt healthcare delivery. Despite the central role of nurses in disaster response, qualitative evidence describing their experiences in isolated contexts remains limited. PURPOSE: To analyze the perceptions and experiences of nurses deployed to respond to a seismovolcanic crisis on an island without a hospital. METHODS: A descriptive qualitative study was conducted between March 2024 and November 2025. Twelve nurses involved in the response participated in semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using interpretive qualitative content analysis supported by WebQDA software. DISCUSSION: Nurses operated under sustained uncertainty, limited situational awareness, and reliance on evacuation pathways. Their roles extended beyond clinical care to coordination, community mediation, and integration into emergency command structures. CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that clearer deployment governance, disaster-specific competency development, and recognition of nursing leadership may support preparedness and health system resilience in geographically vulnerable island settings.

Artificial intelligence tools — large language model chatbots, symptom checkers, AI-based interpretation of wearable-device data, and AI-generated or AI-translated medical content — are increasingly used by patients and families to obtain health information, which they then bring into clinical encounters. This shifts part of nurses' work from providing health information toward identifying, appraising, and calibrating patient-acquired information, including correcting misinformation, addressing questions rooted in AI-generated advice, and negotiating situations where AI-derived information conflicts with professional care recommendations. Two parallel strands exist in the nursing literature: (a) internet-era research on "internet-informed patients" and nurses' responses (L___), and (b) research on nurse–clinical-AI interaction (L___). The intersection — patients' use of AI for health information and nurses' responses — has not been systematically mapped: concept boundaries are unclear, evidence is scattered, and much of it is descriptive or anecdotal. This scoping review aims to map the extent, range, and nature of evidence at this intersection, clarify concepts, describe how nurse responses are studied and measured, and identify evidence gaps to inform practice guidance, health-education strategies, and future primary research. AI-specific evidence is at an early stage; a limited number of eligible Tier 1 sources is anticipated, and a nascent-evidence finding will be reported candidly rather than compensated for by post hoc broadening of eligibility. Citation note: every factual claim in the background must carry an L number; the PMIDs listed in Section 3 are candidate sources, but full citation fields must be completed from the retrieved full texts.

documents.abstract: Metabolic syndrome is a growing global cardiometabolic burden and is increasingly accompanied by demand for continuous, personalized, and evidence-grounded nutrition support. A 2025 systematic review and modelling analysis estimated that 1.54 billion adults were living with metabolic syndrome in 2023, with global prevalence estimated at 28.4% across women and men. Conventional nutrition trackers provide structured quantitative logging, but manual food search, portion selection, and fragmented workflows can increase interaction burden. Large language models (LLMs) provide a natural conversational interface, yet unrestricted generation can produce unsupported nutritional or clinical statements. This paper presents NutriCoach Pro, an agentic nutrition-intelligence architecture that separates deterministic computation, verified food data, evidence retrieval, multimodal perception, and language generation. The system combines a Mifflin-St Jeor energy-estimation engine, activity-adjusted energy expenditure, configurable macronutrient targets, hydration tracking, a bounded Health Compliance Score, deterministic multi-item food parsing, multimodal meal recognition, a sevendomain clinical knowledge base, local retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), optional cloud-model adapters, schema-controlled database actions, and WebSocket-based real-time synchronization. A prototype evaluation plan is defined for NLP extraction, calorieestimation error, unsupported clinical claims, latency, multimodal recognition, and user task performance. Project-reported prototype figures supplied for this manuscript are F1=96.4%, mean absolute calorie error=12.3 kcal, local-RAG latency=42.1 ms, WebSocket synchronization latency=28.4 ms, and unsupported-claim rate below 1.2%; these values are explicitly treated as provisional until reproduced with a documented held-out test protocol. The contribution is an explainable, modular, privacy-oriented architecture that places hard numerical and safety boundaries around generative Al rather than treating an LLM as the source of truth or as an autonomous Clinical decision maker

Using Amazon's and Microsoft's consolidated accounts, it shows how investment can grow faster than cash generation (at Amazon, net capex +81.8% against operating cash flow +28.8% in the twelve months to September 2026). It discusses the Jevons paradox applied to computing, the productivity of installed capacity and the risk of collective overinvestment. This record includes the exploratory dynamic model accompanying the article (Excel, synthetic indices, hypothetical operator, three scenarios for 2026–2030) illustrating how optimistic expectations, indivisibilities and delays can turn shortage into idle capacity. Model results are conditional and are not forecasts for real companies.

documents.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate resident physicians’ knowledge, attitudes, and awareness regarding occupational accidents and to examine factors associated with perceived occupational health and safety competency. This cross-sectional study was conducted among resident physicians working at Necmettin Erbakan University Faculty of Medicine Hospital. A total of 175 resident physicians who voluntarily participated were included. Data were collected using a questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics, occupational accident experiences, and knowledge and attitudes regarding occupational accidents, along with the Occupational Health and Safety Perceived Competency Scale. The majority of residents (86.3%) believed that occupational accidents were not adequately reported.
